neighbours.label: the second half of a correlative comparative, "the X-er ..., the Y-er ..." ("The more you read, the more ...")
fire: The older the wine gets, the more it costs.
The faster she typed, the more mistakes she made.
The more people join the club, the less each of them pays.
The higher we climbed, the colder the wind became.
The more sugar you add, the sweeter the sauce will taste.
The longer the meeting lasted, the more tired everyone grew.
The more carefully you measure, the better the shelves will fit.
The deeper the well, the cleaner the water tends to be.
quiet: The wine is old and it costs a great deal.
She typed faster and made more mistakes that day.
More people joined the club, so each of them pays less.
We climbed higher and the wind became colder.
Add more sugar and the sauce will taste sweeter.
The meeting lasted longer and everyone grew more tired.
Measure more carefully and the shelves will fit better.
The well is deep and the water tends to be clean.

notes: Top examples are mixed function words in conditional or contrastive reasoning. Probes: correlative comparatives 0.36-0.70 (peak in the second clause); the same content in plain coordination 0.01-0.02. Emphatic 'really did/had' also fired (0.36, 0.41), so the label covers a slice.
